criterion_notes.c1: Fails Criterion 1 (and matches Exclusion Criterion 7: water-resource studies unrelated to household or community service access). The study examines basin-level natural resource management and bulk water allocation reform in Australia (particularly the Murray-Darling Basin, sustainable diversion limits, water markets, irrigation, and environmental flows), rather than household or community water or sanitation service access. Although it notes in passing that a 2008 statutory amendment gave allocation priority to critical human needs during drought, household/community water service access is not examined.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording: Yes — the paper examines legal, policy, and governance instruments (three Council of Australian Governments intergovernmental agreements, two Commonwealth policies, the Commonwealth Water Act 2007, the NSW Water Management Act 2000, and the SA Natural Resources Management Act 2004). Narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: No — the paper passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 because it analyzes statutes and intergovernmental governance agreements, but fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading because it evaluates macro-level natural-resource allocation justice intentions (distributive, procedural, and interactive justice keyword frequencies) rather than a rule-type mechanism directly governing household or community water or sanitation service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, tenure/documentation rules, tariffs, enforcement, or utility regulation).
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary empirical text-analytic data via a semiquantitative, descriptive content analysis (keyword coding and weighting verified by independent coders in NVivo and Excel) of eight Australian water reform policy and legislative documents, though no empirical data on household or community service access are collected.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4. The only reported outcomes are Relative Importance (RI) keyword frequency-by-weighting scores representing government social justice intentions across eight policy/legislative texts; no outcome relevant to household or community water/sanitation access, connection, service availability, reliability, continuity, quantity, affordability, or exclusion is measured or reported.
criterion_notes.c5: The unit of analysis (eight Australian federal/interstate/state water reform policy and legislative documents from 1994–2009), analytical dimensions (distributive, procedural, and interactive justice principles), reported measure (Relative Importance keyword scores), and study design (semiquantitative descriptive content analysis) are clearly identifiable.

evidence_quotes.quote: The main strategies of water reform to date have been the establishment and operation of a water market, funding for more efficient water infrastructure, and the creation of planning processes aimed at lowering water extractions.
We applied the framework in a content analysis of eight key policy documents on water reform.
A semiquantitative, descriptive content analysis was used in order to understand government intentions regarding social justice.
The principles with the highest RI scores are assumed to reflect the government’s justice priorities.
The SJF provides a structured approach to include and cross-check justice principles in natural resource policy and strategy.

raw_response.exposure: Social justice principles (distributive, procedural, and interactive justice categories) in Australian federal, interstate, and state water-resource reform agreements, policies, and statutes (1994–2009)
raw_response.outcome: Relative Importance (RI) scores (keyword frequency multiplied by objective-section weighting) representing government justice intentions in water-resource policy documents
raw_response.population_and_sample: Eight Australian water reform policy and legislative documents (three CoAG intergovernmental agreements from 1994, 2004, and 2008; two Commonwealth water policies from 2007 and 2008; the Commonwealth Water Act 2007; the NSW Water Management Act 2000; and the SA Natural Resources Management Act 2004); unit of analysis: policy/legislative document
raw_response.rationale: Excluded as E01 (Wrong topic; see also E04 Wrong outcome and Exclusion Criterion 7: water-resource studies unrelated to household or community service access). The study conducts a semiquantitative content analysis of eight Australian river-basin/natural-resource water reform documents to score government intentions regarding distributive, procedural, and interactive justice in bulk water resource allocation (environmental flows, irrigation, water markets). It does not examine household or community water or sanitation service access (failing c1), does not examine a rule-type mechanism governing service access under the narrow 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 reading (failing c2), and reports only keyword Relative Importance scores in policy texts rather than any service-access outcome (failing c4). Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the decision remains exclude because c1 and c4 are not met.
raw_response.study_design: Semiquantitative descriptive content analysis of policy and legislative documents
